audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for second divine court scene, ha-satan as the Accuser, skin-for-skin idiom, bodily affliction, Job's spouse, Job's refusal to sin with lips, and friends' silent mourning.

verses.restored: Again there was a day when the sons of the Divine came to present themselves before the Eternal, and the Accuser also came among them to present himself before the Eternal.

familiar.text: Again there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came also among them to present himself before the LORD.

verses.restored: The Eternal said to the Accuser, From where do you come? The Accuser answered the Eternal and said, From roaming through the earth and walking around in it.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Satan, From whence comest thou? And Satan answered the LORD, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.

verses.restored: The Eternal said to the Accuser, Have you set your heart on my servant Job? For there is none like him on the earth, a whole and upright man, fearing the Divine and turning away from evil. He still holds fast to his integrity, though you incited me against him to swallow him up for nothing.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Satan, Hast thou considered my servant Job, that there is none like him in the earth, a perfect and an upright man, one that feareth God, and escheweth evil? and still he holdeth fast his integrity, although thou movedst me against him, to destroy him without cause.

verses.restored: The Accuser answered the Eternal and said, Skin for skin; all that a man has he will give for his life.

familiar.text: And Satan answered the LORD, and said, Skin for skin, yea, all that a man hath will he give for his life.

verses.restored: But stretch out your hand now and touch his bone and his flesh, and surely he will bless/curse you to your face.

familiar.text: But put forth thine hand now, and touch his bone and his flesh, and he will curse thee to thy face.

verses.restored: The Eternal said to the Accuser, Look, he is in your hand; only guard his life.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Satan, Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life.

verses.restored: The Accuser went out from the presence of the Eternal and struck Job with severe sores from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.

familiar.text: So went Satan forth from the presence of the LORD, and smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown.

verses.restored: He took a potsherd to scrape himself while he sat among the ashes.

familiar.text: And he took him a potsherd to scrape himself withal; and he sat down among the ashes.

verses.restored: His woman said to him, Do you still hold fast to your integrity? Bless/curse the Divine and die.

familiar.text: Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.

verses.restored: He said to her, You speak as one of the foolish women speaks. Shall we receive good from the Divine and not also receive harm? In all this Job did not sin with his lips.

familiar.text: But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips.

verses.restored: Three friends of Job heard of all this harm that had come upon him. Each came from his place: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite. They agreed together to come to show sympathy to him and to comfort him.

familiar.text: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.

verses.restored: They lifted their eyes from afar and did not recognize him. They lifted their voice and wept; each tore his robe and threw dust toward the heavens over his head.

familiar.text: And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.

verses.restored: They sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and no one spoke a word to him, for they saw that the pain was very great.

familiar.text: So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.
